title: Quick-Apply Recommendation Presets - UX proposal
body:
Purpose and summary:

This doc proposes a compact "quick-apply" UI surface for Optimize recommendations focused on batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization presets. The idea: a lightweight list-first experience that helps engineers scan suggested actions and apply a tested preset in one click, with safe defaults and fast rollback. This is not a replacement for the full recommendation workbench; it's an entry/activation flow aimed at increasing adoption and lowering time-to-value for small teams and product-focused engineers.

Problem we are solving:
- Recommendations are high-value but adoption is low because: exploring details is time-consuming, teams worry about quality regressions, and attaching a rollout strategy is cumbersome.
- Current Optimize screens are dense; customers ask for a quick apply path that minimizes friction.

Target users and scenarios:
- ML engineer wanting to reduce per-token cost for a chat endpoint before a marketing spike.
- Product engineer who wants a safe quantization preset for lower latency on dedicated capacity.
- Platform operator who needs to apply batching for many low-latency routes quickly.

Top-level UX goals:
1) Scanable list of ranked recommendations with compact metrics (estimated cost delta, latency impact, quality risk).
2) One-click "Quick Apply" that creates a controlled rollout (canary + auto-observe) and exposes undo.
3) Expose a compact preview of expected downstream effects (token savings %, P50 change, QA risk label).
4) Keep the heavy configuration in an advanced panel that power users can open.

Proposed screens and interactions (wireframe writeup):

A. Recs Compact List (default view)
- Left column: brief recommendation text (e.g., "Enable batching: group window=128, delay=8ms").
- Middle column: small badges for type (Batching / Caching / Quantize) and model compatibility icons.
- Right column: three inline metric chips: est_cost_delta (-13%), est_p50_latency (+8ms), quality_risk (Low/Med/High).
- Each row: Quick Apply button (primary) and ellipsis menu for More (opens advanced panel).
- Hover behavior: row expands to show 2-line rationale + a link to the prompt-set that generated the recommendation.
- Empty state: CTA to run "Snapshot & analyze" to generate recs.

B. Quick Apply modal (compact)
- Top: short summary of change and the numeric preview (tokens saved per 1M tokens, expected monthly $ saved).
- Middle: rollout selector: Canary (%) with default 10%, target routes (auto-populated with current route), automatic monitor window (default 30m).
- Bottom: Risk checkbox: "Enable automatic rollback on quality regression" (recommended) and a small link "what is regression?" that opens inline docs.
- Confirm button: Apply and run monitors; Cancel.
- Immediately after apply: show toast with Undo (30s) + link to rollout page.

C. Advanced panel (side sheet)
- Shows exact config JSON, compatibility warnings, test prompts for a canary run, and toggle to pin as a preset for the org.
- Expose a slider for quantization aggressiveness and a dropdown for batch window heuristics.

Microcopy and accessibility notes:
- Buttons: use clear verbs: "Quick Apply", "Review details", "Run analysis".
- Risk label color: green/amber/red plus descriptive text; include screen-reader friendly text for risk score.
- Keyboard: support row focus with arrow keys + Enter to open Quick Apply modal.

Backend/API considerations (brief):
- Quick Apply should call a new /optimize/rollouts API that accepts: recommendation_id, rollout_percent, monitor_window, auto_rollback=true/false, treat_as_preset=true/false.
- The UI will receive an immediate rollout_id back and link to trace logs/metrics.
- Estimations must include a confidence band; UI will display a range (e.g., -10% to -16%).

Grooming backlog (initial priorities):
- OPT-QAP-1: Compact list view component + sample data (High, 5)
  Acceptance: list renders 10 rec rows, metric chips populated, keyboard nav works.
- OPT-QAP-2: Quick Apply modal + rollout API contract (High, 8)
  Acceptance: modal applies a rollout to a test route in staging and returns rollout_id.
- OPT-QAP-3: Advanced side sheet with JSON view + preset pinning (Medium, 5)
  Acceptance: user can pin a preset and it appears in org presets list.
- OPT-QAP-4: Inline estimation confidence bands + small explainer (Medium, 3)
- OPT-QAP-5: Auto-rollback experiment wiring and toast/undo UX (High, 8)
- OPT-QAP-6: Accessibility pass and keyboard shortcuts (Low, 2)
- OPT-QAP-7: E2E test harness for canary verification (Medium, 5)
- OPT-QAP-8: Analytics events + funnels for adoption tracking (High, 3)

Suggested acceptance criteria and metrics:
- Adoption: >18% of accounts with generated recs use Quick Apply in 30 days of feature visibility.
- Speed to activation: median time from rec generation to application < 6 minutes (for Quick Apply users).
- Cost impact: measure average per-token cost reduction for applied presets in first 14 days.
- Safety: auto-rollback triggered in <1% of quick applies in experiment cohort.

A/B test plan:
- Variant A (control): existing rec page with single "Review" flow.
- Variant B (treatment): Quick Apply visible, default open collapsed.
- Primary metric: apply rate within 7 days. Secondary: rollback rate, estimated cost savings. Run for 8 weeks or until 2k exposed routes.

Edge cases & constraints:
- For privacy-regulated routes (customer flagged), Quick Apply must surface an additional confirmation and enforce manual review — backend returns a flag and UI greys out Quick Apply.
- Some quantization presets incompatible with KV cache; UI should show explicit incompatibility and disable that combination.

Micro-interaction details (animations & timing):
- Row expand: 120ms fade + 80ms slide.
- Quick Apply modal: 200ms scale-in.
- Toast undo: show for 30s with subtle pulse.

Copy examples (for designers/devs to reuse):
- Row title: "Enable batching (window=128, delay=8ms)"
- Metric chip tooltip: "Estimated monthly cost change for current traffic: -13% ±3%"
- Modal confirm: "Apply preset to route(s) and start a 10% canary with monitoring."
- Undo toast: "Preset applied — Undo?"

Follow-ups and next-phase ideas:
- Add a "multi-apply" mode to apply presets across many routes with templated substitutions.
- Generate suggested canary percentages based on historical traffic variability.
- Surface a small simulator: simulate 24h of traffic to preview actual latency distribution changes.

Open questions (to resolve during grooming):
- Should Quick Apply pin a preset by default? (Pros: easier reuse. Cons: cluttering space.)
- How do we encode quality risk in a transparent, audited way so customers can accept it?
- Should the default canary percent be dynamic or fixed?

Next steps (short term):
1) Design: produce 3 low-fidelity mock variants for the compact list (due 2025-09-19).
2) Eng: align on /optimize/rollouts API and staging contract (due 2025-09-26).
3) Product: finalize acceptance metrics and experiment plan (due 2025-10-02).
4) Cross-functional kickoff meeting: schedule for week of 2025-09-22.

Notes and references:
- Related tickets: OPT-452 (recs engine improvements), OPT-460 (quantize presets).
- See existing Optimize docs for metric definitions and prompt-set linking.

Design attachments (placeholders):
- compact-list-v1.png (attached in Figma)
- quick-apply-modal-v2.png (attached in Figma)

Owner and review: Aisha Morgan (product), review requested from Lina, Marco, Samir, Emily.

End of doc.
